The “ribonucleoprotein particle” that recognizes a newly forming (nascent) polypeptide is the Signal-Recognition Particle (SRP).  

• SRP is an RNA-protein complex.  
• When it binds the signal sequence of a nascent chain emerging from a ribosome in the cytosol, it pauses translation (“Pause there for a minute”).  
• SRP then guides (“Let me show you in”) the ribosome–nascent-chain complex to the rough endoplasmic reticulum, where the chain enters the secretory pathway.  
• In the ER (and later the Golgi) the protein is glycosylated (“you really need some sugar”).  
• Proteins that enter this pathway are usually destined for secretion outside the cell.

Thus, they first meet in the cytosol, and the polypeptide’s ultimate destination is the extracellular space.

Answer: C
